newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. June T-bonds break to downside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. June T-bonds break to downside.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures broke out to the downside and are expected to grind lower for the rest of the shortened week, technical analysts said.
"The technicals that set up in the last couple of days are not helping," one bond futures floor source said.
June T-bonds have proceeded to trade down to 108-17/32 after breaking below 109-00, which corresponds to a cash bond yield of 7.00 percent, at the opening.
"That helps confirm that we are in a near-term downtrend," said David Ging, vice president of Donaldson, Lukin & Jenrette Securities.
Analysts noted the emergence of sell signals in some sentiment indicators last week.
They also noted bearish divergences between prices and both the daily stochastics and relative strength indexes, in both the bond and Eurodollar futures markets.
Some also said June T-bonds' failure to hold gains at 110-22/32, the 2-1/2-month high, last week was a bearish short-term signal.
Technicians said 108-17/32, June's daily low, was significant as it represented both the 50-day moving average and a Fibonacci retracement level.
With their retreat to 108-17/32, June bonds have retraced 50 percent of their April-May rally from 106-12/32, the low of 1997, to 110-22/32, the 2-1/2-month high.
"We should find some short-covering," said Steve Boyajian, director of technical analysis at MMS International.
Boyajian said the near-term trend would remain weak if June is unable to close above 108-30/32. Further support is at the 108-01/32 to 108-00 area, which represents a retracement of about 62 percent.
A close at 108-00 or below would point to a retest of 106-27/32, the lowest level in 8-1/2 months.
Analysts said the U.S. Treasury department's auction of two- and five-year notes on Wednesday and Thursday would weigh on Eurodollars.
They said support is at 93.64 for December Eurodollars and at 93.86 for September Eurodollars.
Boyajian said a decline through 93.64 would point to a drop to the 93.55 to 93.54 area.

They said both contracts were still pricing-in a 25 basis point rate hike by September. December would have to rally to 93.87 and September would have to climb to 94.10 to price-out another rate increase.
